newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: PM Hun Sen warns of trouble if Cambodian prince returns.
newsitem.headline: PM Hun Sen warns of trouble if Cambodian prince returns.

text.p: Cambodian co-Premier Hun Sen on Thursday warned violence could erupt if a prince accused of plotting to kill him decides to return home from exile next week.

Prince Norodom Sirivudh has said he plans to return home for the April 13-16 Cambodia New Year. He was sent into exile in December 1995 after being held one month on charges of involvement in an alleged plot to kill Hun Sen.
First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh has urged his uncle, a member of his FUNCINPEC party, to postpone his return for fear it would aggravate political tensions.

Tensions between the royalists and the Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party have been high since a deadly grenade attack on a demonstration on March 30 led by opposition leader and FUNCINPEC ally, Sam Rainsy.

King Norodom Sihanouk on Monday wrote to Ranariddh saying he would not make an enemy of Hun Sen by granting an amnesty to Sirivudh and said he would resign immediately if the affair was settled in violence.
"If FUNCINPEC and Sirivudh would like to see the king abdicate then Sirivudh might be here," Hun Sen told reporters on his return from an official visit to Laos.
But he warned that if Sirivudh returned, "I propose that the population should not come near (Phnom Penh's) Pochentong Airport.
"I suggest that no FUNCINPEC member should come here (the airport) and use their skin to protect (the prince) because Sirivudh is just a spark that could create a fire."

Hun Sen reiterated that if Sirivudh returned the verdict against him should be applied. He has previously said the prince should serve two-thirds of a 10-year sentence handed down in absentia for his alleged role in a plot to kill him.

Ranariddh, who formed an uneasy coalition with Hun Sen after U.N.-run elections in 1993, said on Wednesday he had advised Sirivudh to postpone plans to return home on April 14 despite calling last month for an amnesty for his relative.
